title: Brauer splitting theorem over a field containing exponent roots of unity
statement: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $N\geq1$, and suppose $K$ contains an element $\zeta$ with $\zeta^N=1$ and $\zeta^j\neq1$ for every integer $0<j<N$. Let $G$ be a finite group such that $g^N=1$ for all $g\in G$. Define $K[G]$ as the $K$-vector space with basis $[g]$ for $g\in G$ and bilinear multiplication $[g][h]=[gh]$. There are integers $r\geq1$, $d_1,\ldots,d_r\geq1$ and a $K$-algebra isomorphism $K[G]\cong\prod_{i=1}^r M_{d_i}(K)$ [def-weil-matrix].

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2, printed p.138, representation-theoretic input cited to Serre 1978, 12 section 2.3 and 13 section 14.4. The auxiliary characteristic-zero splitting-field input is Brauer’s theorem (a field containing the exponent roots of unity is a splitting field); Serre is WANTED and this theorem is left statement-only.
